subject: general
question: A man travels from A to B at a speed of 20 km/h and returns by increasing his speed by 50%. What is his average speed for both trips?
solution:
**Given:**

A man travels from A to B at a speed of 20 Km/h

Returns by increasing his speed by 50%

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total distance / Total Time

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb93b9d711b8962bc13805a6ff8d0beac5f5458bf3b715e1e6d00ece50a66dc5.png] **

Speed of A to B = 20 km/h

Speed of B to A = 20 + (20 × 50/100) = 30 km/h

Time taken from A to B = d/20 hr

Time taken from B to A = d/30 hr

Average Speed = (d + d)/(frac{d){20} + (d)/(30)}

⇒ 24 km/h

**∴ Average speed is 24 km/h**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

Average Speed = (2 times 20×30)/(20+30)

⇒ 24 km/h

∴ Average speed is 24 km/h
